That week of opposite schedules can feel long, especially doing most of the days solo.

A few things that help other parents get through it:

- Split the 24h into clear shifts so you both get one protected block of sleep. For example, your partner takes the baby right after work in the morning while you sleep, then you take over while they get their main sleep before the next night.
- Keep daytime simple - easy meals, a short outing in the morning if you have energy, and an early, calm bedtime routine for the baby so your evening is a bit lighter.
- Leave each other little handover notes about feeds, naps and diapers in the app, so you don't have to wake each other to catch up.
- Plan one small moment to connect each day, even 10 minutes for tea together before they leave or a voice note overnight.

How are you covering nights at the moment - are you doing them all, or splitting?

outcomes.text: my partner and I keep bickering about who does the 3am feed
outcomes.caption:
That 3am feed can feel like the hardest one to share fairly, especially when you're both tired.

Some families find it helps to make it explicit instead of deciding in the moment — for example taking alternate nights, or splitting the night in two shifts so each of you gets one longer stretch, with the other parent fully off-duty and sleeping elsewhere if you can.

It can also help to trade off what happens around the feed, not just who feeds — so nappy, settling and morning wake-up count too. Would you like to talk through what your nights look like right now and find a split that feels fairer for both of you?

outcomes.text: how could we split the nights more fairly?
outcomes.caption:
Splitting it so you decide it once, not at 3am, often helps the bickering fade.

A few ways other parents do it:

- Split the night in shifts, like 9pm-2am and 2am-7am. Whoever is off-duty sleeps undisturbed in another room with earplugs, while the on-duty parent takes all wakes, feeds and settling.
- Take whole alternate nights. One of you is fully on and the baby stays with you, the other is fully off.
- Count the hidden work too. Who does the nappy, the resettle, and who gets up first in the morning all count toward fair.

It helps to rotate weekly so neither of you is always stuck with the harder stretch, and to check in briefly in daylight — not in the night — about what felt fair.

What does a night look like for you two right now — one wake or a few, and do you both have to get up for work in the morning?

For the way back, a small bag within reach can help a lot - a soft teether or rattle, a cloth book, and a spare pacifier if you use one, plus a muslin for comfort and shade.

It also helps to have a fresh diaper and wipes up front, and a change of clothes in case of a leak. If you are driving, a quick cuddle and stretch break halfway often resets the mood.

outcomes.text: the baby monitor keeps dying in the middle of the night
outcomes.caption:
That is so frustrating when you're already half-asleep. A couple of things that help with that:

Keep the parent unit plugged in overnight by your bed, and check that the baby unit is plugged in too rather than running on battery. If yours has a power-saving video-off mode, that can stretch the charge a lot.

It also helps to do a quick charge check as part of your bedtime routine, and keep a spare cable where you charge your phones so you can swap quickly in the night.

Does yours die on both ends, or is it mostly the one by your bed?

outcomes.text: is it worth getting one with a bigger battery, or should we just leave it on the charger?
outcomes.caption:
Leaving it on the charger overnight is usually the simplest fix - most parent units are made for that, and then battery size matters a lot less.

A bigger battery is only really worth it if you move around a lot during the day without an outlet nearby, or you do a lot of naps out at your partner's place or grandparents.

If you keep having to get up to fiddle with it, try keeping the baby unit plugged in all the time too, and dim the screen / use voice-only mode at night.

A warm bath if she enjoys it, then into pajamas in a dim room. A short book with high-contrast pictures or just telling her about your day in a soft voice. Then one or two short songs and cuddles before laying her down.

E tare obositor sa tot negociati asta in miez de noapte, mai ales cand sunteti amandoi epuizati.

Cateva idei care au functionat pentru alti parinti:

- Impartiti noaptea in doua ture, de exemplu unul pana la 2-3 si celalalt dupa. Cel care e liber doarme in alta camera cu dopuri de urechi.
- Alternati noptile: o noapte tu, o noapte partenerul. Sau alternati doar prima trezire.
- Cel care nu s-a trezit noaptea preia dimineata devreme, ca celalalt sa recupereze.

Ati incercat deja vreuna din variante? Cum arata acum trezirile voastre, va treziti amandoi de fiecare data?

outcomes.text: cum am putea împărți nopțile mai corect?
outcomes.caption:
E o intrebare foarte buna, pentru ca "corect" nu inseamna neaparat 50/50 in fiecare noapte, ci ceva care sa va lase pe amandoi cat de cat functionali.

Ganditi-va la ce conteaza cel mai mult pentru voi acum:

- La ce ore sunteti fiecare mai in forma? Unii adorm greu seara dar se trezesc usor dimineata, si invers.
- Cum e cu munca ziua? Daca unul dintre voi conduce mult sau are nevoie de concentrare mare, poate are nevoie de un bloc de somn neintrerupt.
- Cu ce o linistiti noaptea? Daca e alaptata, de exemplu, multi fac asa: tu hranesti, partenerul schimba scutecul, linisteste si adoarme la loc, ca tu sa te intorci mai repede la somn.

O varianta destul de odihnitoare pentru amandoi este sa aveti fiecare un bloc de 4-5 ore legate de somn, in camera separata. De exemplu 21-02 si 02-07. Blocurile legate obosesc mai putin decat aceeasi cantitate de somn fragmentat.

V-ar ajuta sa stabiliti un plan de proba pentru 3-4 nopti si apoi sa vedeti cum v-ati simtit? Spuneti-mi cum impartiti acum si ce program aveti ziua, va ajut sa-l ajustati.
